OkCupid — best app for inclusivity.

But the risks are, of course, higher on certain websites. With a regular merchant website, for instance, you’re only handing over your credit card information (which is very valuable, admittedly), but with a dating site, you’re potentially providing your credit card details plus crucial personal information, from your date of birth and nationality to your address and phone number. That kind of information can heighten the risk — it's very valuable to online scammers who seek to steal it for use or resale.

In a recent development, while this is a risk you take with literally any dating service, AdultFriendFinder is perhaps more vulnerable than most dating sites because of the nature of its content and user base. It’s important to understand any potential security problems.

While NSFW content is permitted on AFF — it's actually encouraged — users are under no obligation to post nude photos of themselves, or get down and dirty on a webcam feed. Many users opt to do so, of course, and while there's no judgment here — let that freak flag fly high and proud, we say — you do risk potentially awkward conversations with family, friends, or co-workers if they happen to stumble across your account. (That would mean they'd have to fess up to being AFF users too, but even so...).

Unfortunately, bad actors can exploit and use your own personal information against you.

“Data from services with adult content or dating services can be especially sensitive for users, because it’s more personal,” warns Larkina. “If fraudsters somehow obtain such private data, they can use it for more ‘efficient’ blackmailing or targeted phishing.” Needless to say, you should be wary of how you use the site and what information you share, especially if you have a public-facing job.

While dating sites now invest heavily in cybersecurity protections, online threats are constant and keep evolving. Hackers eager to discover treasure troves of personal and financial information often target online dating platforms, which can make users feel super vulnerable.

Industry observers note that adultFriendFinder has suffered two major security breaches, which is actually a pretty stellar record of security over its entire 30-year history. In 2016, hackers gained access to the personal information of four million AFF users before the breach was found and stopped. And a larger breach occurred in 2016, affecting some 300 million AFF accounts, including 15 million that had been officially deleted by users but whose data had not been properly expunged from the AFF servers.

According to recent reports, to combat phishing, AFF offers the option to verify your identity with government-issued identification. This verification process is still optional — it's not required when setting up an account. We recommend doing it and setting a search filter to verified accounts only. That way you'll only interact with people who are 100% legit. It's a surefire way to protect yourself against scammers.

While the private information you give AFF (your real name and email address, for example) isn't public-facing, AFF’s dating profiles are public by default, so if you include a picture of your face (as many accounts do), you can be recognized by friends, co-workers, and family members.

And since AFF has suffered two major hacks before, there’s always a chance it could happen again, which could result in your email address and information ending up in a dodgy database.

Does this all mean you should never use AdultFriendFinder, or any dating site? Absolutely not. We're here to help you protect yourself and stay vigilant, not to discourage you from signing up.

Larkina has shared an additional list of best practices to help you mitigate risks while having fun on AFF or any other dating site:.

To protect your accounts, use strong and unique passwords, change them regularly, and if possible, enable two-factor authentication.

In a recent development, be extremely cautious with what you share with strangers, especially when it comes to sensitive information or intimate photos. “Always assess reputational and other risks before posting or sending anything,” cautions Larkina.

When using AFF in particular, limit your interactions to users who have verified their identity.

In a recent development, summing up her advice, Larkina urges online dating service consumers to treat these “platforms as public spaces, not as private ones” as far as possible, and be ever mindful that “every piece of data you provide — email, phone number, username, etc. — becomes part of your digital footprint.” If you’re careful about what you share and who you share it with, you can safely enjoy AdultFriendFinder and any other dating site.

#162402. COP31: No agreement on climate science, disinformation spreading

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (963 w)

COP31: No agreement on climate science, disinformation spreading

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (963 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The annual UN climate conference is the place where countries negotiate the world's intends to limit global warming and adapt to its consequences — and who will pay for climate action as well as damage from storms, floods and droughts.
  • But this year at COP31 in Antalya, an ongoing dispute over the timing of a key assessment of global warming is risking the scientific foundations of global climate action, say observers.
  • "We are extremely concerned about the situation," noted a diplomat with the European delegation who could not speak on the record, adding that it came down to the future of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the world's leading body of climate scientists.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The annual UN climate conference is the place where countries negotiate the world's intends to limit global warming and adapt to its consequences — and who will pay for climate action as well as damage from storms, floods and droughts.

But this year at COP31 in Antalya, an ongoing dispute over the timing of a key assessment of global warming is risking the scientific foundations of global climate action, say observers.

"We are extremely concerned about the situation," noted a diplomat with the European delegation who could not speak on the record, adding that it came down to the future of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the world's leading body of climate scientists.

The IPCC's scientific assessments, published every six to seven years, provide the basis for major international climate agreements, including the 2015 Paris Agreement. The IPCC began evaluating the latest climate science in 1988 and its most recent report was published in 2023.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Researchers should have actually already started work on the next edition but the last plenary session was put on hold in October at the urging of Russia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and Kenya.

"The IPCC finds itself in a difficult situation," a spokesperson from the German Environment Ministry told DW at COP. "We stand ready to help resolve this matter, so that the panel can continue its work. To that end, we are holding many discussions with various countries to explore possible solutions.".

At the core of the dispute is the question of whether future UN climate talks base their negotiations on the latest scientific knowledge — or not.

That's especially relevant for the next "global stocktake," due in 2028, a report card on the world's climate efforts, which will shape action plans for countries around the world to lower planet-heating greenhouse gas emissions.

The European Union, Brazil, the United Kingdom, small island states and several other countries especially at risk of the effects of climate change have called for the IPCC's seventh assessment report to be published in 2028, so it can be used to inform next steps for climate action. The report covers climate protection and impact.

"It's much more difficult without these scientific reports. Otherwise, we're just talking to ourselves or relying on information that's no longer current," stated a delegation source.

But Russia, Iran, India and Saudi Arabia want the IPCC report postponed until 2029, after the global stocktake.

The official reason: the tight timeline would be detrimental to the quality of the research, and could hinder the participation of researchers and governments representing developing countries.

Disagreements over budget issues have also held up the IPCC's work. Among other expenses, the funds are used to pay the travel arrangements for the hundreds of volunteer scientists, especially those from poorer countries, to attend the IPCC sessions.

"No budget means no more IPCC," remarked a member from another delegation, also speaking on condition of anonymity.

It hasn't come to that point yet, but without planning certainty the whole process risks being delayed — along with the climate negotiations that depend on this knowledge.

Researchers with the IPCC, however, have noted the timeline is attainable.

In a recent development, "We have no time to lose," mentioned an open letter released in October signed by more than 100 researchers from 36 countries — including India and China. "We stand committed to continue working to deliver the [seventh assessment report] in a manner that is rigorous, timely and inclusive.".

But while the dispute over the timeline won't alter the scientific findings themselves, it could delay their political impact.

In its pre-COP communications, France accused the countries delaying the report's publication schedule of attempting to "obstruct science in order to lower the ambition of the global stocktake.".

The IPCC isn't a stranger to attempts at political persuasion: At past climate conferences, delegates from many countries have regularly negotiated the exact phrasing of the summary reports intended for policymakers.

Speaking at COP31 on November 17, EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra said it was "fundamental to protect the integrity of climate science and the role of the IPCC as the source of best available science.".

Although there is no vote on the IPCC at COP31, it's possible that its significance and a timeline for the next report will be included in the final declaration of the climate talks, expected this weekend.

The IPCC has been warning for years that disinformation is hindering global climate action. And the struggle for information and control over the narrative in Antalya hasn't just been limited to the IPCC.

This was apparent in a document DW obtained that had been sent anonymously to several less wealthy countries' delegations in the run-up to COP31.

It claimed to explain the nature of Turkey's proposed goals for boosting electrification to 35% by 2035, but went on to misrepresent several core details of the plans to make them seem less appealing to developing countries than they are in reality.

At least two countries confirmed to DW that they had received the document. It did not state where it hailed from and was labeled as an "equity assessment.".

The presentation portrays electrification as a business venture undertaken by wealthy countries at the expense of poorer nations. The International Energy Agency, however, has calculated that developing countries could save around $100 billion (€90 billion) in fossil fuel imports by 2035 through electrification.

According to recent reports, the presentation also gives the impression that all countries must meet fixed electrification targets. In fact, according to the UN, the 35% target represents a global goal, with individual countries free to determine their own national pathways.

This article was originally written in German.

Tech Report: Voyager 1 team, unbowed by communications glitch, celebrates epic 1-light-day distance milestone

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1700 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, PASADENA, Calif.
  • Sources indicate that voyager team members gathered for a press conference about the mission at the Von Karman auditorium here at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) — the first such Voyager event since 1989, when Voyager 1's twin, Voyager 2, flew past Neptune.
  • Industry observers note that "I remember in 1977 I was standing at the Cape watching Voyager launch, and I never thought I would be here today, 49 years later, to celebrate Voyager's one light-day.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, PASADENA, Calif. – NASA's Voyager mission team cheered and wiped away tears here on Thursday (Nov. 19), celebrating a big milestone — Voyager 1 just reached one light-day from Earth, something no other spacecraft has ever done. The excitement persisted despite a communication anomaly that cropped up on the probe, which the team remains confident is temporary.

Sources indicate that voyager team members gathered for a press conference about the mission at the Von Karman auditorium here at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) — the first such Voyager event since 1989, when Voyager 1's twin, Voyager 2, flew past Neptune. The gathering served to celebrate Voyager 1's distance milestone: At 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT) on Wednesday (Nov. 18), the probe reached one light-day from Earth — the distance a photon travels in one day, which is about 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers). That means it now takes a full day for a signal to travel from Earth to Voyager 1, the farthest human-made object out in space.

Industry observers note that "I remember in 1977 I was standing at the Cape watching Voyager launch, and I never thought I would be here today, 49 years later, to celebrate Voyager's one light-day. What an incredible milestone," Voyager project scientist Linda Spilker said during Thursday's event.

While this day and this week have been chock-full of excitement over the distance milestone, the Voyager mission team has been hard at work, as usual, keeping the two nearly 50-year-old spacecraft alive and functioning.

Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, as JPL spokesperson Raquel Villanueva shared at this celebration, on Saturday (Nov. 14), Voyager 1 stopped transmitting science and engineering data. The team has remained in contact with Voyager 1 while investigating the glitch, and they are confident that they'll be able to solve it soon.

"We listen to each spacecraft every day," Voyager project manager Suzanne Dodd told Space.com at the event. Regarding Voyager 1, "we have an anomaly that is not something unseen before," Dodd stated. "We do have a very strong carrier signal. We right now don't have a frame sync, so we're not getting the science or engineering data currently.".

"But if you recall," Dodd added, "one light-day is very far from us. [It takes] 24 hours to get the signal to the spacecraft, 24 hours for the signal to come down, so it takes two days to diagnose anything on the spacecraft … So we can't do anything fast, and the data rates are very low.".

In a recent development, according to Dodd, this anomaly isn't a major cause for long-term concern. Rather, it's likely just part of the natural aging process for spacecraft.

In a recent development, "These spacecraft are old," she mentioned. "All of us old people have our aches and pains, and you know, sometimes it takes longer to stretch out your muscles and remember things, and so we are in a realm where we're going to see more anomalies with Voyager just due to the distance and the age.".

"But we feel Voyager 1, although it's not sending us the telemetry data, it's pointed at the Earth. It's sending us a strong carrier signal, and I'm confident that it won't be too long, and it will send us data back.".

And, for anyone curious how Voyager 1's slower twin Voyager 2 is faring, Dodd shared that it is doing very well on its own journey through interstellar space. "Voyager 2 is very healthy. It's continuing its mission. It has three scientific instruments on it," she told Space.com.

"Each spacecraft is basically setting a record every day for longevity or distance," Dodd added about the twin probes.

It has been revealed that despite the communications anomaly — and even though most of the team had been up all night to confirm the one-light-day signal from Voyager 1 — the room was alive with excitement. The Voyagers have been flying for nearly 50 years on a mission expected to last just five years, so the team was beyond ready to celebrate.

Industry observers note that amidst the more technical updates about the mission and its current status out in interstellar space, the event included footage of Voyager light-day celebrations from around the world. From children cheering on Voyager to iconic landmarks lighting up gold in honor of the mission's Golden Record, the Voyager love echoed around the world in photos and videos. The footage of this international celebration was enough to move Nicky Fox, NASA's associate administrator for the Science Mission Directorate, nearly to tears.

"I actually thought I was going to start sobbing," Fox joked to Space.com after the media briefing. "I think just hearing children's voices and people saying 'We love you, Voyager,' 'Go Voyager' — it just was amazing.".

It has been revealed that and Fox and the mission team members weren't the only ones sharing their love for Voyager. NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins beamed down her own video message to the Voyager 1 spacecraft from the International Space Station, sharing in the celebration.

"Dear Voyager 1," Watkins said. "As an orbiting outpost just 250 miles [400 kilometers] above Earth, we often feel distant yet deeply connected to our home planet. The International Space Station has had crew continuously living off of the Earth for 26 years, seen hundreds of visitors from around the world, and enabled thousands of experiments to advance space exploration.

"While you have been traveling into the unknown for nearly half a century, helping pave our path, together, our two journeys tell a single story of exploration," she continued. "One remains close to home, and the other reaches ever outward. Voyager 1, you have been a beacon of light, a symbol of exploration, a seeker of truth, a carrier of hope, a brave explorer, traveling further than any human hand has ever reached. You represent the very best of what humanity has to offer.

"As you reach a distance of one light-day from Earth, the entire crew of Expedition 75 and people across the planet send you our admiration and our wishes for a safe and continued journey as you begin your post-one-light-day era. There are so many amazing milestones and discoveries to come. You have a universe ahead of you, and you carry with you our collective hopes and dreams. When we look up from Earth, we will always think of you as you continue forward into the great unknown. May you continue shining bright for all of us. Go Voyager 1!" Watkins stated, ending her message with a weightless backflip from aboard the station.

It has been revealed that in concluding the media briefing, the mission team invited those in the room who, over the past 50 years (or more, with one person sharing their excitement having worked on Voyager before it was even called Voyager) have worked on the mission in one way or another, to stand up to a round of applause. With mission team members today ranging from those in their 20s to their 90s, the people behind this enduring mission span many generations.

Sources indicate that interestingly, Fox actually began her light-day celebrations earlier in the week. She, alongside writer/producer Ann Druyan — who was the wife of the late astronomer Carl Sagan, whose work helped create the mission's Golden Record and who took the now-famous "pale blue dot" Voyager image of Earth to the public — together lit up the Empire State Building gold.

It has been revealed that "I was actually very privileged to flick the switch and turn on the Empire State Building lights on Tuesday evening [Nov. 17]," Fox, wearing golden Voyager-inspired nail polish crafted by her daughter, told Space.com. "That was just spectacular … I was there with Ann … we were both so giddy with the excitement of doing it … It was amazing. And then going up and standing underneath and seeing the tower was just really, really special.".

Recent findings suggest that while the room lit up with excitement for Voyager's light-day milestone on Thursday, the team was also brimming with anticipation for what lies ahead. As Voyager hurtles toward another major milestone, turning 50 in 2027, it remains an active science mission, and the team remains hard at work to push the boundaries of exploration with these aging probes.

Recent findings suggest that "Voyager right now — the two Voyagers — they're in an area of space that we've never been into. So every single bit of data that comes back is precious because it's unique," Fox said.

Sources indicate that "Now we're in a region where the sun's influence is a lot different, and we're in this region where we can start to understand: What is it like out past our sun? What is it like in the space between the stars?" Voyager deputy project scientist Jamie Rankin told Space.com. "We're at a very exciting time of starting to connect what we know and what we've seen, living with this star [our sun] to what is out there.".

In a recent development, "What's next? Voyager is just going to keep on going. You know, people sometimes think, 'When's the mission going to end?' It's never going to end," Fox added to Space.com. "Even when we can no longer talk to Voyager, they're both going to keep going … So there's no end for the Voyager mission.".

With a M.S. in Biology, Chelsea has written and worked for institutions including NASA JPL, the American Museum of Natural History, Scientific American, Discover Magazine Blog, Astronomy Magazine, and Live Science. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Diego Simeone beat the record of Luis Aragones, who recorded his final La Liga victory in 2004.

Atletico Madrid's 3-0 victory over Getafe may have been routine, but the win was another landmark in manager Diego Simeone's lengthy tenure at the club.

Sunday's triumph at Estadio Coliseum was the Argentine's 345th La Liga win in his 567th match, surpassing the record for the most victories in the Spanish top flight.

Simeone beat the mark of legendary former Atletico and Spain manager Luis Aragones, who won 344 matches but needed 189 more games to reach that total.

"It makes me happy," Simeone stated of setting the new mark, with his side now third in the table after 10 wins from 13 games.

"I don't usually find many things to be happy about, but there is an incredible amount of work behind this.".

Questioned about the perception that his team are defensive, Simeone said that was a "constant criticism we face".

He added: "I don't place much value on it, but I do take note of it.

"This narrative that we're a defensive team, as if we're always playing solely to defend. You don't win 345 matches just by defending. Is that even possible?".

The 56-year-old has been in charge of Atletico since December 2011, joining the club in an era when Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid and Pep Guardiola's Barcelona were the dominant teams in Spain.

He outlasted the pair of managerial superstars, leading Atletico into a period of consistent success and staying with his side long enough to witness Mourinho's return to Real this summer, 13 years after his initial departure.

Having won the Europa League in May 2012, after his appointment on 23 December 2011, Simeone led Atletico to the European Super Cup title three months later.

He then won the Copa del Rey in his first full season and secured the club's first La Liga title since 1996 - when Simeone was an Atletico player - in the following campaign.

Atletico have established themselves as the third force in Spanish football under his leadership, qualifying for the Champions League in every full season under his charge.

However he has been unable to win European football's premier competition, losing in the final to city rivals Real twice in heart-breaking fashion - in extra-time in 2014 after Real scored a stoppage-time equaliser, and on penalties in 2016.

Simeone's last silverware arrived in 2021 when he won a second Spanish league championship, while he also guided the team to a Europa League and Super Cup double in 2018.

His contract expires at the end of this season with the Atletico fanbase now waiting to see if their manager intends to extend his remarkable victory record into another campaign.

There has been an evolution since Simeone arrived, but his peak came when his players were happy to defend without the ball, deep in their own box. That is how the titles arrived.

He has not found the same effort or quality with a squad built to attack. In the peak years he found the perfect balance between deep defence and counterattack, yet picking it is harder now that his team must take the initiative.

Recent findings suggest that none of that diminishes his legacy. He turned the club's mentality into a winning one and sustained it for over a decade, the two hardest things in football.

After losing a second Champions League final to Real Madrid in 2016 he could have left, but he renewed his energy.

In a recent development, atletico have flirted with Luis Enrique and Unai Emery, yet everyone agrees he goes when he decides. For now, he finds plenty of reasons to stay.

SpaceX Dragon cargo capsule returns to Earth from the ISS

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • SpaceX's 35th Dragon cargo mission has come home to Earth.
  • In a recent development, the robotic Dragon capsule undocked from the International Space Station (ISS) on Friday (Nov.
  • The freighter made its way Earthward over the next 29 hours, ultimately splashing down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on Saturday (Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SpaceX's 35th Dragon cargo mission has come home to Earth.

In a recent development, the robotic Dragon capsule undocked from the International Space Station (ISS) on Friday (Nov. 20) at 12:05 p.m. EST (1705 GMT), while the duo were flying 260 miles (418 kilometers) above western China.

The freighter made its way Earthward over the next 29 hours, ultimately splashing down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on Saturday (Nov. 21) at 5:03 p.m. EST (2155 GMT).

The Dragon debuted Oct. 13, on a mission called CRS-35 because it was the 35th that SpaceX has flown for NASA's Commercial Resupply Services program.

Sources indicate that the capsule arrived at the ISS on Oct. 15, delivering more than 6,300 pounds (2,860 kilograms) of food, scientific gear and other supplies to the astronauts aboard the orbiting lab. It brought a lot of stuff down to Earth, too.

It has been revealed that "Thousands of pounds of cargo are returning from the space station, including research samples that could advance future space exploration and improve life on Earth," NASA officials wrote in an enhancement on Tuesday (Nov. 17).

"The returning research includes a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct scientists used to study vascular aging and cardiovascular disease in space and on Earth," they added.

Dragon is the only cargo craft flying today that's capable of making such downward deliveries. The others — Northrop Grumman's Cygnus, Russia's Progress vehicle and Japan's HTV-X — are all expendable and burn up in Earth's atmosphere to wrap up their first and only spaceflight.

Editor's note: This story was updated at 12:20 p.m. ET on Nov. 20 with news of successful undocking, then again at 8:55 p.m. ET on Nov. 21 with news of splashdown.

When is the Euro 2028 qualifying draw?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The home nations have been allocated their pots for Euro 2028 qualifying.
  • The Euro 2028 qualifying draw will take place on Sunday, 6 December at 17:00 GMT at the International Convention Centre in Belfast.
  • It will form the twelve groups that make up the qualifying group stage; six containing four teams and six containing five teams.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The home nations have been allocated their pots for Euro 2028 qualifying.

The Euro 2028 qualifying draw will take place on Sunday, 6 December at 17:00 GMT at the International Convention Centre in Belfast.

It will form the twelve groups that make up the qualifying group stage; six containing four teams and six containing five teams.

All 54 Uefa member associations will enter qualifying at the group stage.

Despite hosting the 2028 tournament, the UK home nations and the Republic of Ireland must also participate in qualifying rounds.

England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland will host the Euro 2028 tournament.

The 54 teams have been divided into five pots based on their interim overall ranking in the 2026-27 Nations League following the conclusion of the league phase.

Pots one to four contain 12 teams, and pot five contains six teams.

The teams will then be drawn into the 12 qualifying groups, with the four host teams, as well as Northern Ireland, drawn into different groups.

The four winners of the Nations League quarter-finals must be drawn into a group containing four teams.

Twenty teams, made up of 12 group winners and eight best runners-up, will advance directly to the tournament proper. The eight highest-ranking runners-up will be based on the overall qualifying rankings.

If host nations fail to win or are runners-up in their group, there will be two spaces in the tournament proper reserved for the best-ranked nations at the end of the group stage, regardless of how many other host nation teams have qualified.

As a result, the final number of teams in the tournament proper will be between 20 and 22 nations, depending on the performance of the host nations.

There are also qualifying routes available through the 2026-27 Nations League.

Nations League final rankings will also determine the seeding of nations for Euro 2028 qualification.

You can read more on how the process works here.

Pot One: England, Portugal, France, Germany, Spain, Belgium, Netherlands, Norway, Greece, Italy, Denmark, Croatia.

Pot Two: Wales, Serbia, Turkey, Czech Republic, Switzerland, Sweden, Austria, Northern Ireland, Slovenia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Hungary, Republic of Ireland.

Pot Three: Ukraine, Scotland, Kosovo, Poland, Israel, Romania, Georgia, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Albania, Iceland, Slovakia.

Pot Four: Estonia, Belarus, Faroe Islands, Cyprus, Finland, Moldova, Armenia, Bulgaria, Kazakhstan, Luxembourg, Latvia, San Marino.

Pot Five: Malta, Azerbaijan, Lithuania, Andorra, Gibraltar, Liechtenstein.

Matchday three: 11-12 June 2027.

Matchday five: 23-25 September 2027.

Matchday six: 26-28 September 2027.

Matchday seven: 30 September-2 October 2027.

Matchday eight: 3-5 October 2027.

Matchday nine: 11-13 November 2027.

Matchday 10: 14-16 November 2027.

Wembley Stadium will host two of England's group-stage matches should they qualify for the final tournament.

If the host nations and/or Northern Ireland qualify for the tournament proper, they will have dedicated slots at stadiums:.

England (Group B): Etihad Stadium (one match), Wembley Stadium (two matches).

Northern Ireland (Group D): Tottenham Hotspur Stadium (one match), Villa Park (one match), Wembley Stadium (one match).

Republic of Ireland (Group E): Dublin Arena (three matches).

Scotland (Group F): Hampden Park (three matches).

Wales (Group A): Principality Stadium (three matches).

If the hosts and/or Northern Ireland qualify via the play-offs, they will still be assigned to their designated group, but will not play all their group matches in the locations mentioned above.

#162387. Breaking: Einstein was right! Scientists verify 1st image of a black hole ever captured

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (808 w)

Breaking: Einstein was right! Scientists verify 1st image of a black hole ever captured

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (808 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An independent team of researchers has validated the first image of a supermassive black hole captured by humanity.
  • Captured by a global network of telescopes forming an interferometer called the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) and revealed to the public in 2019, the image shows the supermassive black hole at the heart of the galaxy Messier 87 (M87), located 55 million light-years away.
  • The image of this black hole, designated M87*, with a mass around 6.5 billion times that of the sun, was an immense scientific achievement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An independent team of researchers has validated the first image of a supermassive black hole captured by humanity. That, in turn, verifies Einstein's greatest theory, general relativity, which first predicted the existence of black holes and what their immediate surroundings would look like.

Captured by a global network of telescopes forming an interferometer called the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) and revealed to the public in 2019, the image shows the supermassive black hole at the heart of the galaxy Messier 87 (M87), located 55 million light-years away.

The image of this black hole, designated M87*, with a mass around 6.5 billion times that of the sun, was an immense scientific achievement. That may lead to the question: why did it need verifying at all?

Team leader and researcher with Australia's Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO), Samuel Lai explained why capturing the image of a distant black hole is so tricky.

"It is like standing in your backyard and trying to take a photo of a doughnut on the moon," Lai mentioned in a statement sent to Space.com via email.

It has been revealed that lai and his small Australian team developed advanced machine learning and artificial intelligence techniques to capture information about the black hole's structure and filter out interference resulting from the fact that the EHT was viewing M87* from within our planet's atmosphere. The machine-learning technique called GenDIReCT also accounted for biases introduced by combining telescopes to create an Earth-sized interferometer. "When we applied it to the original EHT dataset, we found a black hole almost identical in size and shape as the historic EHT image. Importantly, our model had no idea what a black hole looked like when we applied it to the M87 data," Lai continued. "This is the first truly independent validation of the EHT image, an important step in the scientific process.".

This could settle the questions of just how the final image of M87* was influenced by both atmospheric effects and the processing methods needed to reconstruct pictures from telescope data.

That's not just good news for the EHT; it's good news for Einstein.

Einstein published his theory of general relativity in 1915, completely reshaping how we think of gravity. General relativity suggested that objects with mass curve the very fabric of space and time, united as a single entity called spacetime. Gravity arises from that curvature.

The greater the mass, the more extreme the curvature and thus the greater the gravitational influence of that object. Taking this to its extreme, scientist Karl Schwarzschild came up with a solution to the equations of general relativity that suggested an infinitesimal region with infinite mass, resulting in unrestrained curvature, a singularity. Around this would be a spherical boundary at which not even light has the velocity needed to escape this region. Referred to as the Schwarzschild radius, that boundary became known as the event horizon of a black hole. The singularity, its heart. Black holes were born in 1915, decades before their discovery and over a century before the EHT saw one.

Recent findings suggest that general relativity also predicted what the region around the event horizon would look like. A ring of superheated glowing plasma with the shadow of the black hole falling on it.When scientists first saw the image of M87* they were astounded at how close it reflected predictions made by general relativity, thus confirming the the theory once again. This verification further solidifies that development.

Verifying the EHT's image of M87* could lead to the CSIRO-developed technique being applied to some more "down-to-Earth" uses such as improving medical imaging and mapping earthquakes.

Industry observers note that "Independent validation is at the heart of the scientific process, and it is especially valuable for results as novel as those of the EHT. It is extremely gratifying to see that GenDIReCT, an elegant, entirely independent method, recovers the ring structure of M87* across several years, in excellent agreement with the EHT Collaboration’s published results," Laurent Loinard, Director of the EHT Collaboration, stated.

"Studies like this strengthen our confidence in what we have learned about black holes, and enrich the toolkit available to the whole community.".

In a recent development, the team's research was published on Wednesday (Nov. 11) in the journal Nature.

He also writes about science communication for Elsevier and the European Journal of Physics. Rob holds a bachelor of science degree in physics and astronomy from the U.K.’s Open University. "I feel so f--king alone, and I've never had to sit in this much pain in my entire life," he added. “Imagine having a really horrible toothache that radiates up to your SKULL…. It's so intense that your brain doesn't allow you to think about anything else other than that.".

Big-ticket holiday items may be harder to find as shipping costs rise

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1000 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This holiday season, significant-ticket items are expected to be in short supply with diesel prices near records, trucking rates close to a post-pandemic level and carrying costs hitting multidecade highs.
  • "We are going to have some of the lowest inventory levels on some of these significant-ticket items we have seen in history," said Deborah Weinswig, CEO of retail analytics firm Coresight Research.
  • Weinswig stated retailers she is working with are holding less inventory of big-screen TVs, grills, large consumer appliances like washers and dryers, and other items that take either big amounts of space or cost a lot of money to hold.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This holiday season, significant-ticket items are expected to be in short supply with diesel prices near records, trucking rates close to a post-pandemic level and carrying costs hitting multidecade highs. All of that is forcing many retailers to rethink their holiday inventory strategy.

"We are going to have some of the lowest inventory levels on some of these significant-ticket items we have seen in history," said Deborah Weinswig, CEO of retail analytics firm Coresight Research.

Weinswig stated retailers she is working with are holding less inventory of big-screen TVs, grills, large consumer appliances like washers and dryers, and other items that take either big amounts of space or cost a lot of money to hold.

"It's freight getting it from there to here; it's carrying costs; then it's just the trucking to get it into the stores," Weinswig mentioned. "We're talking three different pieces right here and each is up significantly year on year.".

The surge pricing for supply chain services is being caused by domestic and international policy.

Industry observers note that according to Evercore ISI, the rates for general trucking have increased more than 47% year over year during the week of Nov. 2.

Industry experts say a large factor has been a crackdown by the federal government on non-citizen truck drivers and non-U.S.-based truck drivers operating in the U.S. That has created a capacity crunch that has raised rates and is expected to continue to create upward pressure.

At the same time, fuel surcharges are spiking.

It has been revealed that most transportation providers charge customers an extra fuel surcharge to offset changes in the cost of diesel fuel. That surcharge has spiked 64% year over year, according to Evercore ISI data, as diesel prices have hit upcoming record highs due in part to the U.S.-Israel war with Iran.

And inventory holding costs — or the total expense of storing unsold goods, which could include the costs for capital, service, storage and other risk factors — are closely tied to the yield on the 10-year Treasury note, which exceeded 5% in October and remains at multiyear highs in November.

Collectively, the higher costs could mean bigger discounts for shoppers willing to wait, according to Bill Catania, CEO of logistics technology firm OneRail, which powers same-day delivery for companies such as FedEx and Lowe's.

"You're going to see more discount and price promotions as we get closer to the holiday to liquidate inventory, so they're not having to transfer it or dispose of it or position it some other way," Catania stated.

It has been revealed that retailers are also facing a conundrum in their holiday inventory strategy when it comes to shipping costs versus opportunity costs. In other words, is it worth it to stock up now, or wait it out in hopes that shipping rates will come down some but potentially miss out on having the right product mix?

It's leading to a wait-and-see approach for stocking shelves after early holiday sales in October, executives said.

Sources indicate that UPS CEO Carol Tomé said on the company's earnings call on Oct. 27 that it's "just starting to get peak season forecasts from our customers.".

Similarly, Derek Leathers, CEO of Werner Enterprises, a trucker for big-box stores and major retailers, remarked retailers are cautious.

"When rates are higher and the cost of capital is more expensive, you are going to have a much more intense focus on not having excess inventory," Leathers said.

Sources indicate that still, 2026 holiday sales are expected to top $1 trillion as inflation drives growth and customer spending is expected to remain healthy, according to Bain & Tech giant's annual forecast. Leathers said even with the surge in trucking and shipping rates, he's seeing that retailers are willing to pay up to stock up.

"The bigger concern right now is wanting to make sure they have their capacity locked in. There is way more dialogue around the assurance of having a truck or whatever mode that needs to be secured," Leathers stated. "Not saying they are price insensitive, because they are certainly always concerned about price. But you can't sell it if it's not on the shelf.".

ShipMatrix, a data analytics firm for the logistics industry, forecasts 2.4 billion packages will be delivered during the 2026 holiday peak, a 4% increase year over year.

Sources indicate that it's an increase that will likely lead retailers to increasingly use gig delivery, especially later in the holiday peak. Gig workers allow retailers and delivery companies to adjust to changes in order flow and accommodate surges of last-minute shopping without spending time and money onboarding upcoming team members.

"Gig economy delivery is great. You know, it fulfills fast, but there's better unit economics out there," Catania said.

Industry experts mentioned they also expect to see more retailers use drones for last-mile delivery for smaller items.

A 2024 PwC study forecast that the cost of drone delivery would "drop by more than 70% over the next 10 years, which will not only match traditional last-mile delivery costs, but surpass them and create an inflection point for the industry.".

Amit Regev, CEO of drone organization Flytrex, remarked the company is in active talks with retailers about using drones for holiday deliveries.

"The expectation now is becoming so much more instant," Regev said.

Retailers have been increasing their use of drones. Lowe's in September said it was launching a drone delivery service in partnership with DoorDash and Alphabet's Wing. Amazon earlier this year said it was aiming to offer drone deliveries in nearly 500 U.S. cities and towns by the end of the year.

Flytrex currently delivers for Walmart and a number of restaurants including Little Caesars and Papa John's.

"Customers are looking for that instant gratification," Regev remarked. "So if it takes too long, they might not want to order with you. And from what we are seeing that's a stronger incentive for them to try and test or deploy deliveries using drones.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Steven Pressley says there is a "fragility" in the Dundee squad.

Head coach Steven Pressley has admitted that "at times, I've wanted to crawl under a rock and hide" after Dundee's 8-0 "humiliation" by Heart of Midlothian.

Two days after the Dens Park debacle, Pressley is still adamant he must shoulder the blame - despite winger Alan Forrest earlier saying the "freak" result was down to the players.

Pressley said after the game he was concerned a poor result was imminent and admits he had sensed some complacency within the squad.

"Our strength has been built on cohesion, unity and aggressiveness," said the head coach, who said he was embarrassed by the result but that at difficult times he "seems to find strength from somewhere".

"I think Saturday highlighted exactly what I've been saying - if we get lazy on the hard yards, we're a very vulnerable team.

"We have to be, as I've been consistent all along, at our absolute best to get results.

"I've sensed a little bit of subconscious complacency and my job is to ensure that doesn't seep into their performance.".

Pressley on wanting to 'crawl under a rock', complacency & 'direct' culture.

Hearts bounce back from 'rocky patch' with Dens 'demolition'.

Pressley believes "there is a little bit of fragility in the squad - certain players of huge talent but a little bit fragile mentally" and must now lift them to face a Hibernian side on Tuesday who are hurting from a 4-0 home defeat by Dundee United.

"It's been a difficult 24, 48 hours," he admitted. "There's been a lot of hurt, a lot of embarrassment.

"At times, I've wanted to crawl under a rock and hide on the back of such a disappointing result.

In a recent development, "But I will say this, you know I suffer a lot from vulnerability at times, but for some reason during difficult moments, I seem to find strength from somewhere. I do and I've had to show strength.

It has been revealed that "But we had a good meeting on Sunday. We chatted a lot about the various aspects and hopefully we can start responding to the disappointment.".

Pressley said he knew pre-match "that we're nowhere near as good as people tell us we are" and he had previously tried "various things" to guard against a poor performance.

"I've been trying to introduce a couple of things within their training, within our debriefs on games," he revealed.

"But obviously what I have tried to do hasn't had the right effect and, when you get a performance like Saturday, which lacked that intensity, lacked those hard yards, that's on me because I have to make sure that they're ready for that.".

It was the first time the former Scotland centre-half has suffered such a heavy defeat as a player or manager.

"There's been some really disappointing days, disappointing results, but of course when you're the head coach and it's my responsibility then this ranks as one of the worst," he added.

Recent findings suggest that "I've been in football for nearly 36 years and you think what have I not experienced and then this comes along. It's the great thing about football - it just keeps testing you.

"We have to use days like this as a reminder to ourselves - as a reset moment. I just hope we can bring some pride back to the football club with the right type of performance against Hibs.".

Steven Pressley was left shocked by Saturday's 8-0 home defeat.

  • Boris Rosenfeld indicates DW a photo of him with his daughter Sofia and can't hold back tears.
  • In a recent development, helives in Israel, while Sofia is in Russia.
  • On October 7, a court in Moscow sentenced Rosenfeld to three and a half years in a penal colony.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Boris Rosenfeld indicates DW a photo of him with his daughter Sofia and can't hold back tears. "This was the last time we saw her. Then she left for Moscow, and this whole case began," he indicates.

In a recent development, helives in Israel, while Sofia is in Russia. For more than a month now, she has been behind bars on charges of financing extremism. The case goes back to two donations totaling 2,000 rubles (about $30) to the late opposition politician Alexei Navalny'sAnti-Corruption Foundation (FBK), which the Russian authorities have since designated as extremist.

On October 7, a court in Moscow sentenced Rosenfeld to three and a half years in a penal colony.

Rosenfeld is a prominent ornithologist who has devoted her life to studying and protecting Arcticbirds. "Sofia was an avid young naturalist from childhood. She loved birds, horses and dogs," her father mentioned as he leafed through a photo album.

Sofia was a teenager when the family moved to Israel but she returned to Russia a few years later and now holds both Russian and Israeli citizenship.

She studied biology at Moscow State University and developed a significant scientific career in Russia. Her colleague, Alexandra Panyutina, who now also lives in Israel, explained that Rosenfeld was devoted to her work from an early age.

"Birds and the Arctic are the defining passions of her life," she noted.

Recent findings suggest that rosenfeld was among the first Russian researchers to develop a systematic approach to monitoring migratory bird populations. To support her research, she even developed a special aircraft.

"They could fly at almost the same speed as the birds and observe them from a low altitude," notes Dmitry (name changed), a colleague of Rosenfeld's. "It swiftly became clear that this was a unique method.".

Rosenfeld is considered to be one of the leading figures in Russian ornithology. Her work has extended well beyond Russia and she has been deeply involved in international research projects. In the field of migratory bird conservation, cross-border cooperation is essential.

Helmut Kruckenberg, the head of the German Institute for Wetlands and Waterbird Research (IWWR), mentioned Rosenfeld was highly respected within the international scientific community.

According to recent reports, "She has done an enormous amount for nature conservation and for the protection of Siberian and Arctic species," he said. "What is happening to her is simply beyond comprehension for us.".

It has been revealed that in the summer of 2021, when Russian authorities designated Alexei Navalny's Anti-Corruption Foundation, also known as FBK, as an extremist organization, Rosenfeld was on a remote Arctic expedition without a phone or access to the internet. Therefore, she did not cancel her regular donations to the FBK immediately, doing so only after her return to the Russian capital Moscow.

According to recent reports, her friend Olga (name changed) described Sofia as a person of absolute honesty. According to her, Rosenfeld's donations to Navalny's foundation reflected a genuine desire to fight corruption. Through her work in Russia's regions, she had seen plenty of it firsthand.

"She was never involved in political activism. Her donations were solely intended to support anti-corruption work," noted her father Boris Rosenfeld. "It's unthinkable".

For him and others close to her, the sentence came as a shock. Although prosecutors had requested a five-year prison term, friends and colleagues expected that she would receive a fine at most.

Sources indicate that there were reasons for that expectation. According to calculations by independent media outlet Mediazona, about 85% of convictions in the 225 cases involving donations to Navalny's foundation have so far resulted in non-custodial sentences. Yet Rosenfeld got three and a half years in a penal colony.

Industry observers note that just a few months after Rosenfeld defended her doctoral dissertation in October 2025, her home was searched. She was also subject to travel restrictions. She continued to work but she had to cancel her annual summer expedition to the Arctic.

Even on the day of the sentencing, her conversations with  her colleagues focused largely on science:  "We discussed how the work could continue in Sofia's absence," Olga stated. "But no one really believed she would end up in prison.".

"The only thing we think about now is how to bring her here," Boris Rosenfeld says as he looks at the pictures from Sofia's last visit.

Recent findings suggest that friends and colleagues who spoke to DW say that his daughter never considered leaving Russia, even as the prospect of a prison sentence loomed. "Sofia would never have left. She simply can't imagine life without geese," claims Dmitry.

According to recent reports, now, her family, friends and colleagues are campaigning to have her sentence overturned. More than 1,000 people have signed an appeal to Russia's Presidential Council for Human Rights.

Boris Rosenfeld is also hoping for support from Israel but so far Israeli consular officials have not been granted access to his daughter in detention.

The two continue to write to each other and he is trying to keep his spirits high: "She writes that she's trying to adjust to life in prison, and that it's hard," he notes. "But she's a strong person.".

A 'wow' player - why Ngumoha is already a Liverpool game-changer

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (910 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rio Ngumoha is going to be a 'wow' player for Liverpool - and he indicated everyone exactly what he is already capable of in Sunday's 4-0 win over Manchester United.
  • Recent findings suggest that he made an outstanding assist then added a fine finish, and there is much more to come.
  • Ngumoha has only just turned 18 but he is already a game-changer, someone who gets people excited because he is so hard to stop when he is one-on-one.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rio Ngumoha is going to be a 'wow' player for Liverpool - and he indicated everyone exactly what he is already capable of in Sunday's 4-0 win over Manchester United.

Recent findings suggest that he made an outstanding assist then added a fine finish, and there is much more to come. He plays without fear so he is going to score and make many more goals the same way.

Ngumoha has only just turned 18 but he is already a game-changer, someone who gets people excited because he is so hard to stop when he is one-on-one.

Of course he can frustrate you at times too, but that's what creative and explosive wingers like him do - and it's because he is so talented that everyone wants to see an end product from him every time he gets on the ball.

There were times against United when Ngumoha did not quite deliver, but he is still so young and I would much rather see players like him take too many touches - or try too many things and fail - than be afraid to try them in the first place.

So, if he runs out of play or runs into too many players at times, because teams are doubling up on him like United were, that just highlights how scared they are of him.

His ability means he occupies opposition players - Youri Tielemans was always backing up Diogo Dalot on his wing to try to help him out, but that just meant United were leaving someone else free.

Ngumoha stars as Liverpool thrash 10-man Man Utd.

Sometimes it is actually harder when you are playing out wide against 10 men because you don't get the same amount of space - United were not attacking the same way they would have done with 11, and they were sitting in more.

It has been revealed that yes, Ngumoha ran up the odd blind alley or got outnumbered but that is always going to happen. As he learns, and gets even better, his decision-making will improve too. He will know when to try to go past people or when to find that free man instead.

But he still showed all the bravery you want from a winger against United and, when you keep trying things the way he did, something is going to come off for you.

I look at Bradley Barcola in a similar way to Ngumoha - he can be frustrating but he tries things, and can be brilliant.

For Liverpool right now, one of the biggest positives is the competition they have in wide areas, with those two plus Victor Munoz and Cody Gakpo.

There are other areas of their squad, like left-back or central midfield, where that competition needs to improve, but I don't really worry about the wide attacking areas in the same way.

Sunday was only Ngumoha's second Premier League start of the season, and his first since the opening day.

He maybe only got his chance because Gakpo has a calf problem but, when everyone is fit, it is really exciting that they will all be thinking they have to play their best to push the manager and get in the team.

Andoni Iraola post-match interview - Liverpool v Man Utd.

In a recent development, there were plenty of other positives for Liverpool, too. All in all, Sunday could not have gone much better for them.

United made a woeful start with poor concentration and mistakes which cost them but, from there, Liverpool saw the game out well.

Just because the opposition has a man sent off early on does not mean any kind of victory is a given, let alone a 4-0 win.

Look at how United's 11 men lost to City's 10 in the Manchester derby earlier this season - we've seen many times how good teams can frustrate a side with an extra player like that.

It definitely does not mean you are going to steamroller them, but Liverpool did that and made an abundance of chances to get even more goals.

Days like this are so important for building belief in all their attacking players, especially because they were playing at home, and against their big rivals.

Up until now, it had felt like Liverpool's better days this season had come on the road, but now the pressure and expectation is off them a bit - particularly if, like Ngumoha or Florian Wirtz, you have scored and played well.

I know from experience that, the next time they go back to Anfield, they will be buzzing. You know that the fans are already with you after you've scored against United, and you feel the love a little bit more.

This is the start of a significant week for Liverpool and Iraola will probably make changes against Club Brugge in Belgium on Wednesday, knowing how difficult Sunday's Merseyside derby will be.

Everton is always a tough game but I think Liverpool will enjoy their trip to Hill Dickinson Stadium, and the confidence they will have after beating United will mean they can go there with a really positive mindset.

Danny Murphy was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

Wirtz had a 'significant game, and he shone'.

Jamie Lee Curtis Details Being “Only Surviving” Member of her Family

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1105 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eonline

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jamie Lee Curtis was honest about her birthday blues.
  • As the Freaky Friday actress celebrated her 68th birthday Nov.
  • “The long and winding road,” Curtis wrote in a post on Instagram.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jamie Lee Curtis was honest about her birthday blues.

As the Freaky Friday actress celebrated her 68th birthday Nov. 22, she reflected on the death of her sister Kelly Lee Curtis earlier this year, which made her the only living member of her nuclear family.

“The long and winding road,” Curtis wrote in a post on Instagram. “Another circle around the sun! Today will be the first year, that I am the only surviving family member of my immediate family and my immediate second family. The last in the line. The loss of my sister Kelly in June was a real blow and I feel sad today.”.

Still, Curtis—whose mom Janet Leigh died in 2004, while her father Tony Curtis died in 2010—emphasized the gratitude she has for her life.

“I look back at photographs of me as a child, and I look so stunned to be here at birth, and it carried on through much of my young life, always seemingly startled and slightly concerned,” she continued. “I've worked through a lot of that discomfort, and I'm so happy to be here and have the life I have. Both personal and creative.”.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, Curtis—mom to Annie, 39, and Ruby, 30, with husband Christopher Guest—expressed desire to pass down what she learned from her late loved ones on to her living family members. “What remains for me is the legacy of other humans who forged a path for me to be here through their actions and examples as I hope I am for my own family and of course friends,” the Halloween star continued, “and, as a public person, the millions of people I've involved in my life.”.

And, of course, Curtis knows she is surrounded by love.

In a recent development, “My husband and my daughters and their families and my young grandson, all of whom I get to see today for this life that I love so very much,” the Oscar winner continued. “I wish you all a happy and healthy Thanksgiving and holiday season.”.

For a deeper look into Curtis’ candidness, keep reading….

Amid the chatter surrounding Pamela Anderson and Liam Neeson’s rumored romance, Jamie Lee Curtis quickly shut down any of the Naked Gun stars’ possible detractors.

“With all due respect to pop culture, if love has found [its] way into that relationship—God bless them both—leave them the f--k alone,” the Everything Everywhere All At Once actress told VT in August 2025. “Let them like each other. Both of them have had hardship, and they’re both beautiful human beings.”.

And she further took a moment to heap praise on her Last Showgirl costar Anderson.

“She’s a beautiful person,” Curtis added, “She was fantastic [in the movie], but she’s a beautiful human being.”.

The actress—daughter to the late Tony Curtis and Janet Leigh—hasn’t held back when it comes to sharing how seeing her parents’ later careers has shaped how she views longevity in Hollywood, and why it makes her more intentional about what she takes on.

Recent findings suggest that “I have been prepping to get out, so that I don’t have to suffer the same was as my family did,” Curtis opened up to The Guardian in a July 2025 interview. “I want to leave the party before I’m no longer invited. I witnessed my parents lose the very thing that gave them their fame and their life and their livelihood, when the industry rejected them at a certain age.”.

In a recent development, and she doesn’t want to be hurt in the same way. “I watched them reach incredible success and then have it slowly erode to where it was gone,” she continued. “And that’s very painful.”.

As for her decades long career, Curtis considers herself an “old lady” jokingly adding, “I’m going to die soon.”.

In a recent development, she takes bedtime seriously—and that’s why she doesn’t want to go to a concert in the evening. In fact, she has a proposition for singers.

“I’m challenging musicians to do concerts during the day,” Curtis posited on Today in March. “Why are there no matinees? For instance, I love Coldplay, I would love to go see Coldplay. I would love it, but the problem is I am not going to see Coldplay if they start their show at nine and there is an opening act. I want to hear Coldplay at 1 p.m.”.

As for how the Academy Award winner wants to turn this dream into a reality?

“I think if we filled a stadium of people who want to see a matinee of Coldplay,” she continued, “I think we’re going to start a trend.”.

The Freaky Friday star proved she was a true Californian by leaving film’s biggest night early to satiate her fast-food craving at the beloved West Coast joint.

“FLY IN [check emoji],” Curtis posted on Instagram March 2024 with a photo featuring her getting a meal at In-and-Out, “GET FLUFFED AND FOLDED [check emoji] PRESENT AT OSCARS [check emoji] GO TO @inandout_burger [check emoji] FLY AWAY.”.

Walking Back Her Not-So Marvelous Take on Superhero Movies.

After not holding back by saying a more recent phase of Marvel Cinematic Universe was “bad,” the Knives Out actress subsequently admitted she regretted her comments on the superhero movie franchise.

“My comments about Marvel were stupid and I will do better,” Curtis, who had previously shaded the Doctor Strange movies while promoting her own multiverse movie Everything Everywhere All at Once, wrote on X in August 2024.“I’ve reached out to Kevin Feige and will no longer play in that mud slinging sandbox of competition we call the internet nor will I engage in the toilet paper promotion or game play that is designed for clicks not content or conversation.”.

For Curtis, a negative comment from a cinematographer while filming the 1985 movie Perfect alongside John Travolta resulted in an eye-opening experience with cosmetic procedures.

“He was like, ‘Yeah I’m not shooting her today. Her eyes are baggy,” she remarked on 60 minutes in May. “I was 25. For him to say that was very embarrassing. So as soon as the movie finished, I ended up having some plastic surgery.”.

“That’s just not what you want to do when you’re 25 or 26,” she continued, “I regretted it immediately and have sort of regretted it since.”.

And it influenced the way she views cosmetic enhancements.

Recent findings suggest that “I’ve become a really public advocate,” Curtis explained, “to say to women, ‘You’re gorgeous and you’re perfect the way you are,’ so,…oh yeah. It was not a good thing for me to do.”.

#162371. Key questions as Rangers host Aberdeen & Dundee visit Hibs

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (950 w)

Key questions as Rangers host Aberdeen & Dundee visit Hibs

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (950 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rangers host Aberdeen in one of two Scottish Premiership games on Tuesday.
  • One between two sides looking to recover from embarrassing home defeats, another a match-up between two teams looking to build on decent away victories.
  • All four looking to make their game in hand count in Tuesday's Scottish Premiership double-header.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rangers host Aberdeen in one of two Scottish Premiership games on Tuesday.

One between two sides looking to recover from embarrassing home defeats, another a match-up between two teams looking to build on decent away victories.

All four looking to make their game in hand count in Tuesday's Scottish Premiership double-header.

So what's to look out for as second-top Rangers host Aberdeen and second-bottom Hibernian entertain Dundee?

Just over a fortnight ago, a Rangers win over Aberdeen at Ibrox on Tuesday would have seemed a surefire bet.

The Dons went into the international break on the back of a 4-0 thumping at home to a Hibernian side whose victory lifted them above their hosts and left Stephen Robinson's side sitting in second-bottom place.

With his team only two points clear of bottom-placed Kilmarnock, and with the fans having failed to take the Northern Irishman to their heart, the Dons acted immediately to end his eight-month spell in charge.

They acted similarly swiftly to appoint former Luzern head coach Mario Frick as the fresh man in charge and his promise of "heavy metal football" immediately got a tune out of his players as they blew away Kilmarnock at Rugby Park to end a dismal run of four straight defeats.

Whether or not it was merely the traditional "new manager bounce", only time will tell, but they will certainly be heading to Glasgow with more of a spring in their step after a win that moved them up to eighth.

Given Rangers' two victories over Aberdeen this season, once in the league at Pittodrie and most recently in the League Cup semi-final at Hampden, have been by a single goal, will that renewed confidence and belief from that 4-2 win in Ayrshire be enough to tip the balance of power?

Certainly, everything else points to a home win.

In recent times, Rangers have had a tendency to pass up chances to put pressure on Celtic - and this time a win would take them to within a point of the leaders and reigning champions.

However, Saturday's late winner away to Motherwell suggests the team that Derek McInnes has built is of more sturdy stuff.

That 2-1 win at Fir Park leaves them unbeaten in 13 matches and they are also eight unbeaten at home, having won seven in a row at Ibrox by an aggregate score of 18-2.

McInnes recognises Rangers have yet to dominate games the way he would like, but at least they now appear to have found a way to create the chances that were lacking early in his tenure.

Indeed, Rangers have now scored in every one of their last 27 games in the Premiership and at Fir Park conjured up 29 goal attempts - their highest total in a single league match this season.

To put a spanner in that increasingly well-oiled machine, the Dons will have to end a run of five straight defeats, by an aggregate of 16-2, at Ibrox since their last win there in September 2023.

Overall, they have lost their latest six meetings with the Ibrox side and, to make matters worse, McInnes has won all six of his Premiership home games against Aberdeen since leaving their manager's office, four with Kilmarnock and twice with Heart of Midlothian last season.

Hibs won at Dens Park in August.

Hibs were unable to back-up that aforementioned 4-0 win at Pittodrie as they suffered an identical home hammering against Dundee United on Saturday.

Recently appointed head coach Marink Reedijk admitted he was taken by surprise by what he said was his side's inability to do the "brilliant basics" as he calls them.

A failure to win at home will not have come as a shock to Hibs fans considering they have watched them seven times in a row now at Easter Road without being able to celebrate a victory.

However, this third straight home defeat came on the back of a three-game unbeaten run away from Leith, including that League Cup semi-final derby win over Hearts.

Reedijk refused to concede that Hibs were suffering a home jinx, but he might reconsider if his side falter again on Tuesday considering visitors Dundee are reeling from an even more painful home battering.

Hearts' 8-0 win was the Dark Blues' heaviest-ever top-flight defeat at home and has left head coach Steven Pressley admitting that "at times, I've wanted to crawl under a rock and hide".

While the former Scotland centre-half preferred to shoulder the blame for letting a bit of complacency develop, he echoed his Dutch counterpart by stressing that his side paid for not doing the basics.

In his case, that meant an admission that his squad have a fragile mentality and are not good enough to compete without working their wee cotton socks off.

Pressley is major on psychology, but how will his squad respond to such a public confession at a time when they are visiting a ground where they have not won in 20 visits since October 2001 under Ivano Bonetti?

Indeed, while Dundee are four places and six points above Tuesday's hosts, they have at the moment lost five of their last seven games on the road and, with Hibs having won 2-1 in the reverse fixture at Dens Park in August, are without a win in five meetings with the Edinburgh side.

To change that sorry trend and continue Hibs' home jinx, they will have to improve on Saturday's statistic of failing to even conjure up an attempt on target.

I've wanted to crawl under a rock and hide - Pressley.

According to recent reports, TL;DR: Burger King is launching a Peanuts holiday menu on Dec. 1. It comes packed in a Snoopy Doghouse Box with wearable knit beanies.

Dec. 1 is officially turning into a fast-food holiday turf war. Just days after McDonald’s announced its Home Alone meal with collectible socks for Dec. 1, Burger King fired back with a nostalgia-heavy Peanuts holiday menu launching on the same day.

According to recent reports, arriving at participating U.S. restaurants on Dec. 1 (while supplies last), the limited-time Burger King x Peanuts collab introduces two distinct meals: the adult-sized Peanuts Pack and a Peanuts-Inspired King Jr. Meal. Both meals are served inside a collectible Snoopy Doghouse Box.

Choice of Entrée — A classic flame-grilled Whopper with Cheese or 10-piece Chicken Nuggets served with Woodstock Golden Ranch.

Charlie Brown Loaded Potato Tots — Crispy, coin-shaped tots filled with melty cheese, savory bacon bits, sour cream, chives, and fluffy potatoes.

Medium Soft Drink — Choice of medium fountain beverage.

Snoopy Holiday Beanie — One of two limited-edition Snoopy holiday beanies.

The Peanuts-Inspired King Jr. Meal includes:.

Choice of Entrée — Hamburger, Cheeseburger, or 4-piece Chicken Nuggets.

Side — Choice of Applesauce or French Fries.

Drink — Choice of Milk or Apple Juice.

Peanuts Collectible Toy — One of eight collectible holiday Peanuts toys in every meal, featuring Charlie Brown, Lucy, Linus, Sally, three festive Snoopy designs, and a Snoopy Doghouse packed with custom stickers for decorating.

For collectors, the adult knit beanies and the eight King Jr. Meal toys are especially interesting. Supplies will be limited, and, much like the McDonald's collectible Home Alone socks, fans will scramble to collect them all.

In a recent development, "Peanuts has been part of holiday family traditions for generations, and we can't wait to bring Snoopy and the gang to Burger King this holiday season," said Joel Yashinsky, Chief Marketing Officer, Burger King U.S. and Canada. "At BK, we go all out on partnerships to create fun experiences for everyone — with new menu items, creative packaging and crowns, collectible Snoopy beanies and Peanuts toys and more, we've created something really special. It's holiday fun for all, and we can't wait to welcome families and fans to BK to celebrate throughout the month of December!".

💡 Key Takeaways
